patients.summary: Healthy administrative coordinator who joined the practice in 2023 and in 2025 developed fatigable ptosis, diplopia and chewing fatigue: acetylcholine receptor antibody positive myasthenia gravis with an anterior mediastinal mass. Admitted from neurology at the end of 2025, seen by oncology in April 2026, and had a robotic thymectomy (WHO B2, stage I) after her last practice visit in June 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT, ESTABLISHING CARE

42-year-old woman transferring after her prior PCP retired. Feels well. No complaints today. Here mostly to have a doctor of record and get caught up on screening.

PMH: nothing significant. Has never been hospitalized.
PSH: none.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: mother has Hashimoto's thyroiditis; maternal aunt with rheumatoid arthritis; father with type 2 diabetes. No early heart disease or cancers she knows of.
Social: administrative coordinator, desk job. Never smoked. Does not drink. No drug use. Walks most evenings.
GYN: regular cycles. Last Pap 2021 per her report, normal. Mammogram last year, normal.

ROS: negative in detail - energy fine, no weight change, no visual or swallowing complaints, no dyspnea, no joint swelling, mood good.

Exam: Vitals in flowsheet, BP normal. Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, lids symmetric, EOMI. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged, no nodes. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities without edema. Neuro grossly nonfocal, strength full, gait normal. Skin no concerning lesions.

PHQ-2: 0.

Assessment/plan
1. Health maintenance, healthy adult. Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c (father with T2DM), TSH (thyroid autoimmunity in mother). One-time hepatitis C and HIV screening, she agrees. Screening mammogram ordered. Pap due 2024 - will do at next year's physical. Records requested from former office for vaccine history.
2. Return for physical in about a year. Portal set up at check-out.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Taylor - all of your bloodwork from Wednesday came back fine. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar and A1c, thyroid and cholesterol are all in a healthy range, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative (those are one-time tests, no need to repeat). Nothing to change. Your mammogram order is in; radiology scheduling should reach out.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired muscles, eyelids drooping, chewing gets hard

S: 44F, usually healthy, on no meds. Over roughly three months she has noticed her muscles wear out as the day goes on. By late afternoon her eyelids sag and she catches herself propping her eyes open at her desk; colleagues have asked if she is sleepy. Long meals are a problem - steak or a bagel and her jaw gives out partway through, then recovers if she stops for a few minutes. Double vision comes and goes, mostly in the evening driving home. All of it is better in the morning and after rest. Denies headache, numbness or tingling, recent illness, weight loss, chest pain. No new medications or supplements.

PMH none. Meds none. NKDA. FH: mother Hashimoto's, maternal aunt RA, father T2DM. Never smoker, no ETOH.

O: vitals in flowsheet, unremarkable. Alert, conversant, speech normal this morning. Mild ptosis, slightly more on the right. Pupils equal and reactive. EOM full at the start of the exam, no diplopia elicited in primary gaze. Neck flexion weak at 4/5; shoulder abduction, grip, hip flexion full. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric. Sensation intact to light touch and vibration. Gait normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P:
1. Fatigable ptosis, diplopia and chewing fatigue with neck flexor weakness, normal reflexes and sensation - this looks like myasthenia gravis until proven otherwise.
- AChR binding antibody, CK, ANA, TSH, CBC, CMP.
- Chest X-ray to look at the thymus region.
- Referral to the neurology EMG lab for repetitive nerve stimulation, and neurology consult.
- Ophthalmology for the double vision.
- No driving if she sees double; reviewed warning signs - trouble swallowing liquids, choking, or shortness of breath means the ED, not a phone call.
- Holding the August physical for now; we will see each other plenty.

reports.text: PA and lateral views of the chest. No prior chest imaging for comparison. On the lateral view there is a rounded soft-tissue opacity filling the retrosternal clear space in the anterior mediastinum. On the frontal view a smooth bulge projects along the left mediastinal contour. Trachea midline. Heart size normal. Lungs clear without consolidation or nodule. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Osseous structures unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Anterior mediastinal mass. CT chest with contrast recommended for further characterization.

documents.title: Chest X-ray Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Anterior mediastinal mass on CXR. In the setting of suspected MG, thymoma is the main concern. Will get CT chest once the antibody and nerve stimulation results are in, and call her today so she hears it from me. Called - she was calm, understood plan.

documents.title: Blood Test Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Taylor, the rest of your bloodwork is back. The acetylcholine receptor antibody is positive at 7.6 - this is the antibody we see in myasthenia gravis and fits your symptoms. Your muscle enzyme (CK) is normal and the ANA screen is negative, and thyroid, blood counts and chemistries are normal. The nerve stimulation test on 8/6 will help confirm. I know this is a lot; I'm glad to talk by phone any time this week.

documents.title: RE: Blood Test Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you for explaining. I read a little about it tonight. Is the chest thing connected? I'll keep the 8/6 appointment.

documents.title: RE: Blood Test Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Possibly - growths of the thymus gland can go along with myasthenia, which is why we'll get a CT. One step at a time; I'll call after the 8/6 test.

reports.text: Indication: fatigable ptosis, diplopia and chewing fatigue; AChR antibody positive. Skin temperature maintained above 32 C. Routine motor and sensory nerve conductions of the right median, ulnar and sural nerves: normal latencies, amplitudes and conduction velocities. Repetitive nerve stimulation at 3 Hz: decrement of 22% recording nasalis (facial nerve), 16% recording upper trapezius (spinal accessory nerve), and 7% recording abductor digiti minimi (ulnar nerve), within normal limits. Repair of decrement after brief exercise in trapezius. Limited needle EMG of deltoid and first dorsal interosseous: normal.
reports.conclusion: Abnormal study. Decremental response to slow repetitive stimulation in facial and proximal muscles, consistent with a postsynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder such as myasthenia gravis. No evidence of neuropathy or myopathy.

documents.title: EMG Laboratory Report
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Received by fax from outside neurology group EMG laboratory.

Patient: Taylor Pickett. Date of study: 08/06/2025. Referring: primary care.
Allergies: NKDA.

Repetitive stimulation shows a clear decrement in facial and trapezius recordings (22% and 16%), hand normal. Routine conductions and limited needle exam normal. Interpretation: postsynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder, consistent with myasthenia gravis, in the context of positive AChR antibody. Patient is on the clinic waitlist for a neuromuscular consult. Reasonable to start pyridostigmine for symptoms in the interim; happy to discuss.

Scanned to media; PCP notified.

medications.sig: Take 1/2 tablet (30 mg) by mouth up to 3 times daily as needed for chewing or eyelid weakness

orders.reason: anterior mediastinal mass on chest X-ray, myasthenia gravis

documents.title: Results and Plan
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with nerve stimulation results - decrement in face and shoulder muscles, together with positive AChR ab this confirms myasthenia gravis. Spoke with the reading neurologist this morning: fine to start pyridostigmine at low dose for symptoms while she waits for the clinic. Rx pyridostigmine 60 mg tabs, half tab (30 mg) up to TID as needed, ideally 30-45 min before meals. Side effects reviewed: cramping, loose stools, sweating, extra saliva. CT chest with contrast ordered for the mediastinal mass. Neurology referral already placed - she is waitlisted. Again reviewed red flags (swallowing liquids, choking, breathing) - ED. She repeated plan back.

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast. Comparison: chest radiograph 07/23/2025. In the anterior mediastinum there is a well-circumscribed, homogeneously enhancing soft-tissue mass measuring 3.8 x 2.9 cm in axial dimensions. Fat planes with the pericardium, great vessels and sternum are preserved; no evidence of invasion. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary lymphadenopathy. No pleural or pericardial effusion. No pleural nodules. Lungs clear. Airways patent. Thyroid unremarkable. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. No osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: 3.8 x 2.9 cm well-circumscribed anterior mediastinal mass without signs of invasion; thymoma favored given the clinical history of myasthenia gravis.

documents.title: CT Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Taylor, your CT shows a smooth, well-defined growth in the front of the chest, about 3.8 cm, with no sign that it is pushing into anything around it. With your myasthenia the most likely explanation is a thymoma, a growth of the thymus gland. Neurology will guide next steps for both. Their scheduler called us: first opening with the neuromuscular specialist is Wednesday 12/31. I've asked to be notified of any earlier slot. How is the pyridostigmine going?

documents.title: RE: CT Result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: December feels far away but ok. The half pill helps at dinner if I remember to take it ahead of time. I only take it once most days, sometimes not at all.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OPHTHALMOLOGY CONSULTATION - received by fax 9/24/2025
Date of visit: 09/19/2025
Referred by: primary care, for diplopia and ptosis

Dear colleague,

Thank you for sending Ms. Pickett, 44, now about two months from her first visit with you. She describes double images that come and go and lids that sink lower toward evening. Since July chewing and swallowing solid food have become harder as the day wears on, and she gets a little winded with exertion such as stairs. No recent illness. She takes pyridostigmine 30 mg as needed, rarely more than once a day.

Meds: pyridostigmine 30 mg PO PRN. Allergies: NKDA. No surgical history.

Exam: VA 20/20 OD and OS with correction. Pupils equal, briskly reactive, no APD. Lids: ptosis that increases with sustained upgaze; she could not hold upward gaze beyond 30 seconds before the lids fell and she reported doubling. Ocular alignment orthophoric in primary gaze at the start of the exam. Anterior segments quiet, lenses clear. Dilated fundus exam: healthy discs and maculae, normal vessels and periphery OU. Of note, rising from a squat she needed to push off with her hands; otherwise strength was full this morning and reflexes normal.

Data reviewed: CK normal and ANA negative on your July labs; CT chest with an anterior mediastinal mass.

Impression: fatigable ptosis and intermittent binocular diplopia from ocular involvement of known myasthenia gravis, with proximal and bulbar fatigue suggesting generalized disease. Eyes otherwise healthy.

Plan: no prism or lid procedure while symptoms fluctuate. Lid crutch or taping can help on long days. Management per neurology. Glad to see her again as needed.

Ophthalmology

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY CLINIC NOTE - received 1/6/2026 with discharge summary
Date of visit: 12/31/2025
Reason: myasthenia gravis, referred by primary care

HPI: 44-year-old woman seen for myasthenia gravis diagnosed this summer (AChR binding antibody positive, decrement on repetitive stimulation), with workup to date through her PCP and ophthalmology over the past five months. For several months her stamina has steadily worsened over each day - chewing, talking at length, and climbing stairs all wear out. After eating she often has to rest because the jaw tires. Double vision in the evenings. No recent infection, chest pain, or sensory symptoms. She uses pyridostigmine 30 mg only occasionally and takes nothing on a daily basis.

PMH: myasthenia gravis; anterior mediastinal mass on CT 8/2025. PSH: none. Allergies: NKDA. FH: mother Hashimoto thyroiditis, maternal aunt RA, father T2DM. Social: never smoker, no alcohol or drugs.

Exam: vitals stable. Mild ptosis bilaterally that worsens after 30 seconds of sustained upgaze. Ocular movements full in range but fatigue with prolonged testing. Strength 5/5 at the start of the visit; after repeated shoulder abduction proximal arm strength falls to 3/5. Reflexes present and symmetric. Sensation intact.

Labs today: unremarkable.

Assessment: generalized AChR-positive myasthenia gravis, progressing, with bulbar fatigue; anterior mediastinal mass concerning for thymoma.

Plan: given progressive bulbar and proximal weakness on minimal treatment, admit today for workup and initiation of therapy. Inpatient CT chest to evaluate for thymoma. Neurology will follow while inpatient.

Neuromuscular neurology

events.reason: Generalized myasthenia gravis, workup and initiation of therapy

medications.sig: 1.5 mg IM 30 minutes before the evening meal
Take 1 tablet (60 mg) by mouth up to 4 times daily as needed, 30-45 minutes before meals

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast. Comparison CT 08/11/2025. The well-circumscribed homogeneous anterior mediastinal soft-tissue mass now measures 4.0 x 3.0 cm (previously 3.8 x 2.9 cm), otherwise unchanged in character. Preserved fat planes with pericardium, great vessels and sternum; no invasion. No pleural or pericardial nodules or effusion. No lymphadenopathy. Lungs clear.
reports.conclusion: Anterior mediastinal mass, 4.0 x 3.0 cm, consistent with thymoma. No evidence of local invasion or pleural spread.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received 1/6/2026)
Admitted: 12/31/2025 from neurology clinic. Discharged: 01/03/2026.
Allergies: NKDA.

Reason for admission: progressive generalized AChR-antibody-positive myasthenia gravis with bulbar fatigue, for workup and start of therapy.

Hospital course: Breathing and swallowing were monitored throughout; she managed a regular diet and had no respiratory difficulty. Neostigmine 1.5 mg IM was given before dinner on the day of admission as initial therapy; within the hour her double vision cleared and she chewed her meal without stopping. Over the next two days she was transitioned to oral pyridostigmine 60 mg before meals with sustained benefit. CT chest 1/1: 4.0 x 3.0 cm anterior mediastinal mass consistent with thymoma, no invasion. CBC, BMP, TSH and magnesium normal.

Discharge diagnoses: myasthenia gravis, generalized; anterior mediastinal mass, suspected thymoma.

Discharge medications: pyridostigmine 60 mg PO up to four times daily as needed, 30-45 minutes before meals (replaces prior 30 mg as needed).

Follow-up: hematology/oncology referral placed for the mediastinal mass. Neurology clinic in 3 months. PCP within 2 weeks. Return for difficulty swallowing, choking or shortness of breath.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after her 12/31-1/3 admission from the neurology clinic (summary reviewed). The injection before dinner the first night made a striking difference, she says - first meal in weeks without stopping to rest her jaw. Now on pyridostigmine 60 mg before meals as needed; most days takes it before lunch and dinner, skips breakfast dose. Eyelids still droop some evenings, double vision much less. Back at work.

Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg PO up to QID PRN (30 mg PRN discontinued). NKDA.

Exam: vitals fine, weight steady. Ptosis minimal at 3:30 pm. EOM full without diplopia on brief testing. Neck flexion 5-/5. Speech normal. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. Myasthenia gravis, generalized, improved on pyridostigmine. Med list reconciled. Neuro f/u 3 months.
2. Anterior mediastinal mass, 4.0 cm on inpatient CT, suspected thymoma - hem/onc referral from the hospital is in process; she has not heard yet, front desk to call and confirm it was received.
3. RTC after the oncology visit or sooner.

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HEMATOLOGY/ONCOLOGY CONSULTATION - received 4/24/2026
Visit date: 04/20/2026
Referral: inpatient neurology team, for anterior mediastinal mass

Ms. Pickett is a 45-year-old administrative coordinator seen after evaluations with her PCP, ophthalmology and neurology. Over roughly the past year she has had worsening fatigue, with lids that drift down and chewing that tires during longer meals; it is worse toward evening and eases with rest. She has had no trauma, fevers or weight loss, and no neurologic illness before this. She takes pyridostigmine 60 mg as needed before meals and no scheduled medications.

PMH: myasthenia gravis (AChR antibody positive). PSH: none. Allergies: NKDA. FH: mother Hashimoto thyroiditis; maternal aunt rheumatoid arthritis; father type 2 diabetes. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: well appearing. Eye movements show weakness that fluctuates during the exam; mild dysarthria as she talks. Limb strength full at rest but fades with repeated effort. Sensation and reflexes intact. No cervical or supraclavicular adenopathy. Lungs clear; heart regular.

Data: CMP today without metabolic abnormality. Chest radiograph today: widened mediastinum from the known mass. CT 1/1/2026: 4.0 x 3.0 cm well-circumscribed anterior mediastinal mass without invasion (3.8 x 2.9 cm in 8/2025).

Impression: anterior mediastinal mass in a patient with AChR-positive myasthenia gravis, radiographically consistent with thymoma, apparently encapsulated and resectable.

Recommendations: no biopsy needed given the typical appearance and resectability. Referral to thoracic surgery for thymectomy, which also serves the myasthenia. We will review the pathology and arrange follow-up afterward.

Hematology/Oncology

documents.title: Thoracic Surgery Consultation
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
THORACIC SURGERY CONSULTATION (outside) - received by fax 5/14/2026
Seen 05/12/2026 at the request of hematology/oncology.

45F with AChR-positive generalized myasthenia gravis and a 4.0 cm anterior mediastinal mass on CT, consistent with thymoma, without signs of invasion. Myasthenia currently controlled on as-needed pyridostigmine; no swallowing or breathing problems. No prior surgery. NKDA. Never smoker.

Exam: well, speaking comfortably, mild lid droop. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

Assessment/plan: resectable thymoma with myasthenia - complete thymectomy indicated. Plan robotic-assisted thymectomy on 06/18/2026 with planned 1-2 night stay. Discussed risks including bleeding, phrenic nerve injury, conversion to open, and post-operative myasthenic weakness. Neurology aware and will confirm she is stable for surgery. Please see her for preoperative medical evaluation within 30 days of surgery and fax your note.

Thoracic Surgery

documents.title: Preoperative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pre-op medical evaluation
Procedure: robotic-assisted thymectomy, 6/18/2026, thoracic surgery. Anesthesia: general.

S: Doing reasonably well. Pyridostigmine 60 mg before lunch and dinner most days, occasionally a breakfast dose on long workdays. Lids still tire by evening; double vision now uncommon. Chewing ok with the pre-meal dose. No trouble swallowing liquids, no choking, no shortness of breath. Walks 20-30 min most evenings without chest pain or undue breathlessness - easily more than 4 METs. No prior anesthesia. No personal or family bleeding problems. No recent illness.

Meds: pyridostigmine 60 mg PO up to QID PRN. Allergies: NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

O: vitals reviewed, normal; weight stable. Mild bilateral ptosis appearing toward the end of the visit. EOM full. Speech clear. Neck flexion and proximal strength 5/5. Airway: normal mouth opening and neck motion. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

PHQ-2: 1.

A/P
1. Preoperative evaluation: low-risk patient for an intermediate-risk procedure. No cardiac testing needed; no ECG indicated. CBC and BMP today, will fax with this note.
2. Myasthenia gravis - stable on PRN pyridostigmine. Anesthesia should be aware of MG (neuromuscular blockers, post-op weakness); surgeon reports neurology is coordinating peri-op plan. Continue pyridostigmine through the morning of surgery unless told otherwise.
3. Thymoma - surgery 6/18.
4. Health maintenance: turned 45 this year. Colorectal screening discussed; she prefers stool testing for now - FIT kit given. Mammogram due in the fall.

Follow up after recovery from surgery.

documents.title: Pre-op Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count and chemistry panel from yesterday are normal. My note and the labs were faxed to the surgeon's office this morning. Best of luck on the 18th - please send me a message when you're home.

documents.title: Clearance Faxed
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pre-op note and 6/4 labs faxed to thoracic surgery. Confirmation received.

reports.text: Specimen: thymus and anterior mediastinal mass, thymectomy. Gross: encapsulated tan-pink lobulated mass 4.2 x 3.4 x 2.6 cm within thymic fat; cut surface lobulated with thin fibrous septa; no necrosis or hemorrhage grossly. Microscopic: thymoma composed of polygonal epithelial cells admixed with abundant immature T lymphocytes, with perivascular spaces. Capsule intact; no capsular invasion. Surrounding thymic tissue and fat without tumor. Margins negative. Immunohistochemistry: epithelial cells keratin-positive; lymphocytes TdT-positive.
reports.conclusion: Thymoma, WHO type B2, 4.2 cm, encapsulated without capsular invasion (Masaoka-Koga stage I). Margins negative.

documents.title: Surgical Discharge Summary
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - THORACIC SURGERY (received with pathology 6/26/2026; filed)
Admission 06/18/2026 - discharge 06/20/2026.
Allergies: NKDA.

Procedure 6/18: robotic-assisted thymectomy with en bloc resection of the anterior mediastinal mass. No complications; minimal blood loss. Neuromuscular blockade avoided per anesthesia plan.

Course: extubated in the OR. Monitored for myasthenic weakness with serial bedside checks - none; swallowing and breathing normal throughout. Pyridostigmine resumed the evening of surgery. Chest tube removed POD 1. Walking the halls by POD 1. Discharged home POD 2.

Pathology: thymoma, WHO type B2, 4.2 cm, encapsulated, margins negative, Masaoka-Koga stage I.

Discharge medications: pyridostigmine 60 mg PO up to 4x daily as needed (unchanged); acetaminophen as needed for incision pain.

Follow-up: thoracic surgery clinic in 2-3 weeks; neurology in August; oncology to review pathology.

documents.title: FIT Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Message to pt: normal, repeat yearly. Also got her surgical discharge summary today - home on POD 2, path stage I.

documents.title: Thoracic Surgery Post-op Visit
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
Thoracic surgery clinic, post-op visit 07/07/2026 (received 7/9/2026).

Three weeks after robotic thymectomy. Port sites healed, no drainage. Minimal discomfort, off acetaminophen. Breathing comfortable; walking daily. Myasthenia symptoms no worse than before surgery.

Pathology reviewed with her: thymoma WHO B2, stage I, completely resected. No adjuvant radiation or chemotherapy recommended. Surveillance CT chest yearly, first due 6/2027; oncology following.

Cleared for full activity and return to work. Return as needed.

Thoracic Surgery

documents.title: Pyridostigmine Refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy refill request for pyridostigmine 60 mg. Last fill 6/2026 per fill history, using about 2-3 tabs/day. One refill sent per PCP protocol; neurology appointment 8/10, asked pt to have neurology take over the prescription.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neuromuscular clinic follow-up 08/10/2026 (outside; received 8/13/2026)

Seven weeks after thymectomy for a stage I type B2 thymoma. She notes easier meals and less evening lid droop since surgery, and fewer pyridostigmine doses on some days. No swallowing or breathing difficulty.

Exam: trace ptosis after prolonged upgaze; eye movements full; neck flexion and proximal strength full with repetition today; speech normal.

Impression: AChR-positive generalized myasthenia gravis, improved after thymectomy.

Plan: continue pyridostigmine 60 mg up to four times daily as needed; we will prescribe going forward. Further improvement after thymectomy can take months to years. Return in 3 months.

Neuromuscular neurology

documents.title: Update After Surgery
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just an update - back to full days at work since the end of July and feeling better than I have in a year. Neurology said they'll handle the pyridostigmine now. Question: the surgeon said a CT every year - do I schedule that with you or with them?

documents.title: RE: Update After Surgery
documents.author: RN
documents.body: So glad to hear it, Taylor. The yearly scan is ordered by oncology/thoracic surgery, so their office will set it up for next June. Your doctor will see the update in the morning.
